title: Risk Assessment: Wire full-stack integration tests into CI and SDLC pipeline
summary: Assessment of the architect's recommended approach (A+C): Phase 1 adds pull_request triggers to lint.yml, test.yml, and test-integration.yml; Phase 2 adds orchestrator-managed DinD sidecar for SDLC self-testing. Phase 1 is low-risk with high confidence — 4 additive workflow file changes on well-understood GitHub Actions infrastructure. Phase 2 carries substantially higher risk due to privileged container management, DinD reliability, image pre-loading complexity, and changes to core orchestrator code. Recommend proceeding with Phase 1 immediately and deferring Phase 2 to a separate issue with dedicated human review.

risk_assessment.overall_verdict: Proceed with Phase 1 (Option A) — low risk, high value. Phase 2 (Option C) should be a separate issue due to its high complexity and security implications requiring dedicated architecture review.
risk_assessment.confidence: High — based on source code analysis of all 4 affected workflow files, 8 test files (4216 lines), both compose stacks, container_spawner.py (650 lines), devserver.py (1029 lines), docker_client.py, sandbox Dockerfile, and network configuration.

risks.title: Integration tests flaky or failing on ubuntu-latest due to aarch64→x86_64 architecture mismatch
risks.description: All 91 integration tests were developed and validated on Linux 6.17 aarch64 (Asahi/Fedora). GitHub Actions ubuntu-latest runs x86_64. The test infrastructure involves Docker image builds (gateway from gateway/Dockerfile, orchestrator from orchestrator/Dockerfile, mock-sandbox from integration_tests/local_pipeline/mock-sandbox/Dockerfile), compose stack orchestration with hardcoded subnets (172.40.0.0/24, 172.41.0.0/24), health check timeouts (120s each for gateway and orchestrator at conftest.py:295,309), and container lifecycle management. Architecture-specific issues (different Docker storage driver behavior, kernel capabilities, network namespace handling, timing differences) may cause failures that don't reproduce locally.
mitigation: Start integration tests as non-required PR checks (architect's TD-5). Monitor for 5-10 successful runs before promoting to required.
Run test-integration.yml manually via workflow_dispatch on a test branch BEFORE enabling the pull_request trigger — validate the full compose stack works on ubuntu-latest x86_64.
The conftest.py already has generous timeouts (120s health check, 300s compose up, 120s mock-sandbox build). If CI is slower, increase pytest timeout to --timeout=600.
If architecture-specific failures appear, add `platform: linux/amd64` to compose service builds to catch multi-arch issues early.
risks.rollback: Remove pull_request trigger from test-integration.yml. Lint and test workflows are independent and unaffected.

risks.title: Docker subnet conflicts on shared CI runners
risks.description: Both compose stacks use hardcoded subnets: integration_tests/docker-compose.yml (172.40.0.0/24, 172.41.0.0/24) and integration_tests/local_pipeline/docker-compose.yml (same subnets). If multiple CI jobs from different PRs run concurrently on the same runner, subnet conflicts cause compose to fail with 'network already exists' errors. The conftest.py uses dynamic COMPOSE_PROJECT_NAME (conftest.py:204) to namespace services, but Docker networks with explicit IPAM cannot coexist at the same subnet on a single daemon.
mitigation: GitHub-hosted runners (ubuntu-latest) are isolated VMs with separate Docker daemons. Concurrent PR runs get different runners. Risk is negligible for hosted runners.
If self-hosted runners are used later, replace hardcoded subnets with Docker's auto-allocated subnets (remove IPAM config) or use unique per-run subnets derived from GITHUB_RUN_ID.
The existing docker network prune -f in cleanup mitigates orphaned networks.
risks.rollback: N/A — no code change needed for this risk. Monitoring only.

risks.title: Integration tests add significant CI time to every PR
risks.description: The integration test workflow must: build 3 Docker images from scratch (gateway, orchestrator, mock-sandbox — no Docker layer caching configured), start a compose stack, wait for health (up to 120s per service), run 91 tests with 300s timeout, then tear down. No caching is configured — only release-images.yml uses docker/setup-buildx-action. Every PR push triggers a full uncached rebuild. On ubuntu-latest cold Docker cache, total workflow time could be 10-15 minutes. Currently none of the three test workflows have concurrency groups, so rapid pushes stack CI runs.
mitigation: Add path filtering to the pull_request trigger from the start. Only run integration tests when gateway/, orchestrator/, shared/, integration_tests/, docker-compose.yml, or Dockerfile changes are detected. This avoids wasteful runs on docs-only or config-only PRs.

Add concurrency groups with cancel-in-progress: true to all three workflows to cancel stale runs on rapid pushes. Pattern: concurrency: { group: '${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.ref }}', cancel-in-progress: true }.
Add Docker layer caching via actions/cache (pattern available from release-images.yml:118) to speed up image rebuilds.
Pre-build images as explicit CI steps (architect's task-1-3) to get clearer failure reporting than relying on the compose --build flag.
risks.rollback: Add path filtering retroactively if CI time becomes problematic. No breaking change.

risks.title: Autofix workflow (on-check-failure.yml) depends on fragile workflow name coupling
risks.description: on-check-failure.yml:8 watches for workflow_run events from workflows named exactly 'Lint' and 'Test'. The architect proposes adding 'Integration Tests' (task-1-4). This coupling between workflow names is undocumented and fragile — renaming any workflow without updating on-check-failure.yml silently breaks autofix. More critically, the autofix bot is designed for lint and type errors (it invokes reusable-autofix.yml which uses the egg action for code fixes). Integration test failures are typically Docker/compose infrastructure issues, not code issues amenable to automatic fixing. The autofix bot attempting to 'fix' a compose timeout would waste resources and potentially make incorrect code changes.
mitigation: Defer adding 'Integration Tests' to the autofix watcher (skip task-1-4 initially). Evaluate after integration tests are stable whether autofix is useful for Docker-related failures.

Add a comment to the top of lint.yml, test.yml, and test-integration.yml documenting the on-check-failure.yml dependency: '# WARNING: Workflow name is referenced by on-check-failure.yml. Do not rename without updating that workflow.'
If autofix is added for integration tests, ensure reusable-autofix.yml can gracefully handle cases where it cannot fix the failure (exit cleanly rather than making speculative changes).
risks.rollback: Remove 'Integration Tests' from on-check-failure.yml workflows list.

risks.title: Dual triggers (workflow_call + pull_request) may cause double execution
risks.description: Adding pull_request alongside workflow_call means each workflow runs autonomously on PR events. If any future workflow later calls them via workflow_call on pull_request events, tests run twice per push. Currently no callers exist, but this is a maintenance awareness risk for future developers.
mitigation: Document the dual-trigger design in a workflow comment: 'Runs both as reusable workflow (workflow_call) and directly on pull_request. Do not create a separate caller workflow for PR events — use Option A, not Option B (see issue #647).'
No technical mitigation needed — risk is architectural awareness only.

risks.title: DinD sidecar requires --privileged, introducing first privileged container in orchestrator (Phase 2)
risks.description: docker:27-dind-rootless still requires elevated privileges (--privileged or specific capabilities + /dev/net/tun device access). The orchestrator currently never creates privileged containers — DevserverManager explicitly sets privileged: false and cap_drop: ['ALL'] at devserver.py:288-295. DinD would be the FIRST privileged container the orchestrator manages, breaking a security invariant. If the orchestrator has a bug or is compromised, a privileged container on the host Docker daemon could escape sandbox isolation. The issue notes --privileged + --device /dev/net/tun was validated on the development host.
mitigation: Phase 2 MUST be a separate issue with explicit security review and an ADR documenting the decision to introduce privileged containers.
DinD container must have strict resource limits matching DevserverManager patterns: CPU 1.0, memory 512m, PIDs 256.
DinD container must run on a dedicated isolated internal network — not egg-isolated or egg-external.
Auto-kill DinD container after a strict timeout (e.g., 10 minutes) regardless of test completion status.
Audit log all DinD container creation/destruction events.
Gate DinD behind an explicit pipeline configuration flag (integration_test_enabled), not implicit role detection.
Evaluate alternatives to --privileged: Sysbox runtime, user-namespace remapping, or running integration tests only in CI (Phase 1) without DinD.
risks.rollback: Revert DindManager module and container_spawner changes. Phase 2 is fully independent of Phase 1.
risks.review_reason: First privileged container in the orchestrator breaks an existing security invariant (devserver.py:295 explicitly sets privileged: false). Needs ADR-level review.

risks.title: DinD TCP endpoint (port 2375) is unauthenticated by default (Phase 2)
risks.description: Docker daemon on TCP port 2375 is unauthenticated. The tester sandbox connects via DOCKER_HOST=tcp://dind:2375. If the DinD container is reachable from any other container on overlapping networks, those containers could issue arbitrary Docker commands against the nested daemon — running containers, mounting volumes, or accessing the test network. While the nested daemon only contains test infrastructure, it provides an escalation path for network reconnaissance or data exfiltration.
mitigation: DinD container MUST be on a dedicated, internal-only Docker network that only the specific tester sandbox is attached to. No other containers should be able to reach the DinD TCP endpoint.
Use TLS-authenticated Docker (port 2376 with DOCKER_TLS_CERTDIR) instead of plain TCP (2375). DinD supports automatic certificate generation.
Network policy: firewall rules or iptables within the DinD network to restrict access to the tester container's IP only.
risks.rollback: Remove DinD sidecar. Phase 2 is independent.
risks.review_reason: Unauthenticated Docker daemon endpoint on the host Docker network. Need to confirm network isolation is sufficient.

risks.title: DinD image pre-loading is fragile, slow, and resource-intensive (Phase 2)
risks.description: The architect proposes pre-loading images via `docker save | docker -H tcp://dind:2375 load`. This means: (1) serializing each image to tar on the host daemon (CPU + disk I/O), (2) transferring over TCP to the DinD daemon (network I/O — images can be 200-500MB each), (3) deserializing inside DinD (CPU + storage). Three images (gateway, orchestrator, mock-sandbox) means potentially 1+ GB of transfer. Over TCP on a Docker bridge network, this may take 2-5 minutes. If the TCP connection drops mid-transfer, partial image state in DinD causes confusing test failures. The DinD daemon's storage backend (overlay2 inside overlay2) adds latency.
mitigation: Use shared volume mount between host Docker and DinD for image transfer instead of TCP pipe. Save images to a shared volume, then load from the volume inside DinD — avoids network transfer entirely.
Implement per-image verification after each load: confirm image exists with `docker images` on the DinD daemon.
Add retry logic (1-2 retries per image) with exponential backoff.
Set per-image transfer timeout (120s per image).
On any pre-load failure, DindManager MUST tear down the DinD container and report a clear error — never leave a partially-loaded daemon running.
risks.rollback: DindManager cleanup should always remove the DinD container regardless of pre-load success/failure.

risks.title: container_spawner.py is critical-path code — Phase 2 modifications are high-risk
risks.description: container_spawner.py (650 lines) manages the container lifecycle for EVERY pipeline agent. spawn_agent_container() (lines 192-461) handles gateway session registration, network config, volume mounts, extra_hosts, and container IP assignment. Phase 2 requires modifying this function to conditionally provision a DinD sidecar for tester agents. Any bug in this conditional path could affect ALL container spawning (not just tester agents) if the condition check is incorrect or if shared state is accidentally mutated. The function already has complex branching for network modes (public/private/local) and mount configurations.
mitigation: Keep DindManager as a completely separate module with its own lifecycle — container_spawner.py should only have a thin integration layer calling DindManager.start()/stop().
DinD provisioning MUST be triggered by an explicit flag in pipeline config, not inferred from agent role. This prevents accidental DinD for non-test scenarios.
Write comprehensive unit tests for the DinD integration path BEFORE modifying container_spawner.py.
Code review must verify the non-DinD path (99% of spawns) is completely unaffected — no shared mutable state, no new parameters on the hot path.
Consider a wrapper pattern or pre/post hooks rather than if/else branching inside spawn_agent_container().
risks.rollback: Revert container_spawner.py changes. DindManager module can remain as dead code.
risks.review_reason: Critical-path orchestrator code. Bug here affects all pipeline agent spawning.

risks.title: test-integration.yml cleanup step is incomplete — orphaned containers and networks possible
risks.description: Current cleanup (test-integration.yml:39-42) only runs `docker compose -f integration_tests/docker-compose.yml down -v --remove-orphans` — the gateway-only stack. It does NOT clean up the local_pipeline compose stack (integration_tests/local_pipeline/docker-compose.yml). If local pipeline tests fail mid-execution, containers and networks from the local_pipeline stack remain orphaned. Additionally, the conftest.py fixture has its own teardown, but if pytest itself crashes or the CI job is cancelled, the fixture teardown won't run. The conftest.py also cleans orphaned sandbox containers (_cleanup_orphaned_containers) but only at setup time.
mitigation: Add local_pipeline compose cleanup to the CI workflow's cleanup step: `docker compose -f integration_tests/local_pipeline/docker-compose.yml down -v --remove-orphans 2>/dev/null || true`.
Add orphaned sandbox container cleanup: `docker ps -a --filter 'label=egg.pipeline.id' -q | xargs -r docker rm -f 2>/dev/null || true`.
These are defense-in-depth for when the conftest fixture's own teardown fails or doesn't run.
risks.rollback: N/A — cleanup improvements are always safe and beneficial.

risks.title: conftest.py fixture subprocess calls may not honor DOCKER_HOST in DinD mode (Phase 2)
risks.description: The local pipeline conftest.py (line 202-221) passes os.environ to compose subprocess calls, which includes DOCKER_HOST if set. However, the mock-sandbox build step (lines 240-252) does NOT explicitly pass env — it relies on the default os.environ. If DOCKER_HOST is set (DinD mode), the `docker build` command for mock-sandbox would target the DinD daemon, but the image may need to be built on the host daemon first and then transferred. The fixture's implicit environment propagation creates ambiguity about which Docker daemon each command targets.
mitigation: Phase 2: make Docker daemon targeting explicit in every subprocess call. Use DOCKER_HOST=unix:///var/run/docker.sock for host operations and DOCKER_HOST=tcp://dind:2375 for DinD operations.
Pre-build images on the host daemon and transfer to DinD (architect's TD-4), then skip the mock-sandbox build step in the conftest when DOCKER_HOST is a TCP endpoint.
Add integration test: verify conftest fixture works correctly in both host Docker and DinD modes.

phase_1.verdict: Proceed. All changes are additive (adding pull_request triggers), use well-understood GitHub Actions patterns, and are independently reversible. Each workflow can be rolled back individually.
recommendations: Validate test-integration.yml via workflow_dispatch on a test branch BEFORE merging the pull_request trigger. This catches aarch64→x86_64 issues pre-merge.
Start integration tests as non-required checks. Promote to required after 5-10 consecutive green runs across different PRs.
Add path filtering from the start to avoid unnecessary CI runs on docs/config-only PRs.
Add concurrency groups with cancel-in-progress to all three workflows.
Defer task-1-4 (autofix integration) — integration test failures are rarely auto-fixable.

phase_2.verdict: Defer to a separate issue. DinD introduces the first privileged container in the codebase, modifies critical-path container_spawner.py, adds unauthenticated TCP Docker endpoints, and requires complex image pre-loading. Each of these deserves dedicated security and reliability review.
recommendations: Create a follow-up issue for Phase 2 with explicit security review requirements and an ADR.
Prototype DindManager as a standalone module with integration tests before touching container_spawner.py.
Evaluate TLS (port 2376) instead of plain TCP (port 2375) for the DinD endpoint.
Evaluate whether CI-only integration tests (Phase 1) eliminate the need for DinD entirely — if tests gate PRs via GitHub Actions, the SDLC pipeline's tester may not need to independently re-run them.
Issue #645 already references DinD for deployment validation — coordinate Phase 2 work with that issue to avoid duplicated infrastructure.

phase_3.verdict: Proceed alongside Phase 1. Documentation-only changes with no risk.
recommendations: Document the CI workflow naming dependency and test infrastructure setup.

areas_requiring_human_review.area: Phase 2 security model: introducing privileged DinD containers to the orchestrator
areas_requiring_human_review.reason: The orchestrator currently enforces privileged: false on all spawned containers (devserver.py:295). Phase 2 would be the first exception. This breaks a security invariant and needs ADR-level architectural review. The --privileged flag grants the container nearly full host capabilities.
areas_requiring_human_review.decision_needed: Accept privileged container risk with mitigations (resource limits, network isolation, auto-kill timeout) OR investigate alternatives (Sysbox runtime, CI-only testing without DinD, registry-based image distribution).

areas_requiring_human_review.area: Phase 2 scope: implement in this issue vs separate issue
areas_requiring_human_review.reason: Phase 1 (CI integration) and Phase 2 (DinD self-testing) are architecturally independent. Phase 1 provides immediate value with low risk. Phase 2 adds significant complexity and security implications. Combining them in one issue delays Phase 1 value delivery and dilutes review focus on Phase 2 security concerns.
areas_requiring_human_review.decision_needed: Implement Phase 2 in this issue (#647) or create a follow-up issue? Note: issue #645 already references DinD for deployment validation.

areas_requiring_human_review.area: Integration tests as required PR checks — promotion criteria
areas_requiring_human_review.reason: The architect recommends starting as non-required (TD-5). The promotion criteria should be explicitly defined before implementation: how many clean runs, across how many different PRs, who authorizes promotion, and what happens if flakiness is discovered after promotion.
areas_requiring_human_review.decision_needed: Define promotion criteria: N consecutive green runs across M different PRs before making integration tests a required status check.

areas_requiring_human_review.reason: The autofix bot (reusable-autofix.yml) is designed for lint and type errors. Integration test failures are typically Docker, compose, or timing issues — not code issues the bot can fix. Adding integration tests to the watcher risks irrelevant or incorrect autofix commits on PRs.
areas_requiring_human_review.decision_needed: Include 'Integration Tests' in on-check-failure.yml watcher now, or defer until autofix effectiveness for Docker failures is evaluated?

Q1_required_checks.architect_question: Should integration tests be required PR checks immediately?
Q1_required_checks.risk_analyst_position: No. Start informational. These tests have never run in CI — environment differences between local aarch64 and CI x86_64 are likely to surface issues. The test infrastructure has 120s health timeouts and 300s compose timeouts that may be insufficient on shared CI runners. Promote after demonstrating stability.
Q1_required_checks.risk_if_wrong: If made required immediately and tests are flaky: all PRs blocked, development velocity stops. If kept informational too long: untested code merges — but this is already the status quo, so no regression.

Q2_autofix_integration.architect_question: Should autofix watch for integration test failures?
Q2_autofix_integration.risk_analyst_position: Defer. Integration test failures are infrastructure problems (Docker, compose, networking), not code problems. The autofix bot making changes in response to a compose timeout is wasteful at best and harmful at worst.
Q2_autofix_integration.risk_if_wrong: If added prematurely: autofix makes irrelevant commits on integration failures. Low severity — autofix should be idempotent, but noisy PRs erode developer trust.

Q3_phase2_scope.architect_question: Is Phase 2 in scope for this issue?
Q3_phase2_scope.risk_analyst_position: Strongly recommend Phase 2 as a separate issue. Phase 1 alone delivers the primary value (tests gating PRs in CI). Phase 2 introduces 4 High/Medium security and reliability risks (R-6, R-7, R-8, R-9) that warrant focused review. Issue #645 already covers DinD for deployment validation — coordinate rather than duplicate.
Q3_phase2_scope.risk_if_wrong: If combined: Phase 1 delivery delayed by Phase 2 complexity; security review diluted. If separated: minor tracking overhead of two issues.

Q4_path_filtering.architect_question: Should integration tests only run on relevant file changes?
Q4_path_filtering.risk_analyst_position: Yes, implement path filtering from the start. Without it, every PR (including docs, config, CLAUDE.md changes) triggers 10-15 minutes of Docker builds and integration tests. Suggested paths: gateway/**, orchestrator/**, shared/**, integration_tests/**, docker-compose.yml, **/Dockerfile.
Q4_path_filtering.risk_if_wrong: Without filtering: CI waste on every PR, compounding with existing on-pull-request.yml and contract-verify.yml workflows. With filtering: small risk of missing regressions from unlisted paths — mitigated by periodic manual full runs via workflow_dispatch.

recommended_implementation_order: 1. Run test-integration.yml via workflow_dispatch (manually) to validate all 91 tests pass on ubuntu-latest x86_64 BEFORE any workflow changes.
2. Add pull_request triggers to lint.yml and test.yml — lowest risk, immediate value, independent of integration tests.
3. Fix test-integration.yml: add orchestrator + mock-sandbox image builds, add local_pipeline compose cleanup, add path filtering, add concurrency group. Then add pull_request trigger.
4. Add concurrency groups to lint.yml and test.yml.
5. Monitor integration test stability across 5-10 PRs with tests as non-required checks.
6. Promote integration tests to required check after stability confirmed (human decision).
7. Defer Phase 2 (DinD) to a separate issue with security review, coordinating with #645.

agreement: Option A (add PR triggers directly) is correct — Option B (caller ci.yml) breaks the on-check-failure.yml autofix naming dependency. Confirmed by reading on-check-failure.yml:8.
Pre-building images in CI (TD-2) is correct — provides better caching and failure reporting than relying solely on conftest fixture builds.
Option C (DinD sidecar) is the only viable Phase 2 approach that preserves the sandbox trust model. Option D (orchestrator runs tests) correctly rejected for violating trust boundaries.
docker:27-dind-rootless (TD-3) is the right image choice. Rootless reduces attack surface.
TD-5 (non-required checks initially) is the right call — tests have never run in CI.
DevserverManager (TD-6) is good architectural precedent for DindManager — same trust model (orchestrator manages infrastructure, sandbox only runs code).
Phases are correctly identified as independent — Phase 1 provides full value without Phase 2.
concerns: The architect's R-2 ('integration tests add 5-10 minutes to every PR') underestimates impact because it doesn't account for the lack of Docker layer caching or concurrency groups. Without path filtering, EVERY PR triggers this, including trivial doc changes.
Missing risk: the architect doesn't flag that the test-integration.yml cleanup (line 41) only cleans the gateway-only compose stack, not the local_pipeline stack. This should be fixed in task-1-3.
The architect's recommendation to add 'Integration Tests' to autofix (task-1-4) should be deferred — the autofix bot is designed for lint/type errors, not Docker infrastructure failures.

Phase 2 risks are correctly identified (R-3, R-5 in architect output) but undersized. The privileged container risk is not just 'Medium' — it's the first breach of the orchestrator's no-privileged-containers invariant.
Missing: no mention of concurrency groups in any workflow. Rapid pushes will stack CI runs without cancel-in-progress.
additional_risks_identified: R-10 (incomplete cleanup) — cleanup only covers gateway-only compose, not local_pipeline compose
R-11 (DOCKER_HOST propagation) — conftest subprocess calls have implicit env propagation that creates ambiguity in DinD mode
Concurrency groups — none of the three workflows have concurrency settings, causing stacked runs on rapid pushes
